I would say wooden spoons, a good cutting board, and flour sack towels. Not sure if the flour sack towels have a different name in UK, but they are cheap, you can use them to dry dishes, polish and clean glass/chrome, put them over a bowl of bread dough to help it rise, so many things.

Wooden spoons last forever as long as you handwash them, otherwise, they splinter. They're the best for making brownies and sauces, in my opinion, and won't scratch cookware.

Any chef's knife will do, as long as you sharpen it before each use and handwash it. I bought a set from a wholesale restaurant store for $30 about 10 years ago, and they're still in great shape (look for NSF stamp - you'll know they're commercial quality).

A notebook and a nice pen to serve as a journal. With what you've been through, it may help to write. I've been in a similar situation, and it was very therapeutic for me.

Something that makes you, you. It could be a musical instrument, yoga mat, satin chemise to lounge in, a pair of earrings, lipstick, a nice apron, a "signature scent". Whatever makes you feel your most feminine, and something you can always have around. This, other than cast iron/stainless cookware, furniture and linens, is what I'd invest in.

I know the last two aren't really "bottom drawer" things, but I feel like they are things every woman needs. The other two comments have covered a lot of the "musts" in terms of running a household; mine are just suggestions to make you your best for the household.
